q: How do I edit a file in place with sed and keep a copy of the original?
expl: -i.bak saves the original first. Plain -i changes the file with no way back.
ch: Edit in place, with a backup

q: Which command prints only lines 10 to 15 of app.log?
expl: Without -n, sed prints every line, and the range twice.

q: The `url` line in app.conf contains 8080 twice. What does this print?
expl: Without the `g` flag, `s` replaces only the first match on each line.

q: What does the `g` at the end of `s/8080/9090/g` do?
expl: `g` means global: all matches on each line. Without `-i`, the file itself still stays unchanged.
opts: Replaces every match on the line, not just the first one

q: Type a `sed` command that changes `port=8080` to `port=9090` in app.conf in place, saves the original as `app.conf.bak`, and leaves `admin_port` alone.
expl: The caret `^` anchors the pattern at the start of the line, so `admin_port=8080` (and the `?port=8080` in the url) stay as they are.
ch: Edit in place, with a backup

q: You run `sed -i '/#/d' app.conf` to remove the comment lines. Which other line disappears?
expl: `/#/` matches a hash anywhere in the line. Use `/^#/d`, and try it without `-i` first (or with `-i.bak`).
opts: The `url=` line, because it contains a `#` too
None, only lines that start with `#` are deleted

q: Type a `sed` command that prints app.conf without the comment lines (the ones that start with `#`) and without empty lines.
expl: `d` deletes matching lines; `^#` means “starts with a hash” and `^$` is an empty line. Chain them with `;` or `-e`.
`2d` deletes the second line and `$d` the last one.

q: Type a `sed` command that prints only the part of app.log from the `--- START deploy` line to the `--- END deploy` line.
expl: `-n` turns off automatic printing, and `/START/,/END/p` prints every line from the first marker to the second.

q: Why does the lesson write `sed 's|/var/www|/srv/www|'` with `|` instead of `/`?
expl: `s` can use almost any character as the separator. With `/` you'd need `s/\/var\/www/\/srv\/www/`.
opts: The text has slashes in it, so another separator saves escaping each one
`|` sends the result to another command
